bibliographic_label: Patrick J. McNamara. The Arithmetic-Cosmic Structure Conjecture (ACSC) Monograph.
annotation: Original May 2025 manuscript, 121 pages, supplied local PDF; source SHA-256 is recorded in the front matter and revision manifest. Historical manuscript, not an independently validated source of ACSC conclusions.

Protocol/source records, not independent physical evidence.

bibliographic_label: Joseph H. Silverman (2009). The Arithmetic of Elliptic Curves, second edition.
annotation: Graduate Texts in Mathematics 106, Springer. Arithmetic reference for minimal models, heights and isogenies. https://doi.org/10.1007/978-0-387-09494-6

bibliographic_label: J. S. Milne (2021). Elliptic Curves, second edition.
annotation: World Scientific; author-hosted text. Arithmetic background and BSD formulation. The consulted PDF's bibliographic page gives 2021. https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/EC2.pdf

bibliographic_label: Christophe Breuil, Brian Conrad, Fred Diamond and Richard Taylor (2001). On the modularity of elliptic curves over Q: wild 3-adic exercises.
annotation: Journal of the American Mathematical Society 14, 843-939. Modularity theorem, not BSD or ACSC. Author-hosted paper: https://virtualmath1.stanford.edu/~conrad/papers/tswfinal.pdf

bibliographic_label: David Cohen-Steiner, Herbert Edelsbrunner and John Harer (2007). Stability of Persistence Diagrams.
annotation: Discrete & Computational Geometry 37, 103-120. Conditional bottleneck stability. https://doi.org/10.1007/s00454-006-1276-5

bibliographic_label: Frederic Chazal, Vin de Silva, Marc Glisse and Steve Oudot (2012 preprint). The structure and stability of persistence modules.
annotation: Algebraic stability framework. https://arxiv.org/abs/1207.3674

bibliographic_label: Primoz Skraba and Katharine Turner (2020 preprint; consulted revision 7, 2025). Wasserstein Stability for Persistence Diagrams.
annotation: Wasserstein results require their own finiteness and perturbation assumptions; the manuscript does not replace them with an unconditional bottleneck assertion. https://arxiv.org/abs/2006.16824v7

bibliographic_label: Pratyush Pranav et al. (2017). The topology of the cosmic web in terms of persistent Betti numbers.
annotation: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society. Cosmic-web topology methodology. https://arxiv.org/abs/1608.04519 ; https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stw2862

bibliographic_label: G. Wilding et al. (2021). Persistent homology of the cosmic web. I. Hierarchical topology in Lambda-CDM cosmologies.
annotation: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society. Cosmic topology and hierarchical structure in a specified cosmological setting. https://arxiv.org/abs/2011.12851 ; https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stab2326

bibliographic_label: Thierry Sousbie (2011). The persistent cosmic web and its filamentary structure. I. Theory and implementation.
annotation: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society. Persistence-based cosmic-web extraction, distinct from equating beta_1 with filament number. https://arxiv.org/abs/1009.4015

bibliographic_label: Brittany Terese Fasy, Fabrizio Lecci, Alessandro Rinaldo, Larry Wasserman, Sivaraman Balakrishnan and Aarti Singh (2014). Confidence sets for persistence diagrams.
annotation: Annals of Statistics 42(6), 2301-2339. Statistical uncertainty, under the paper's sampling assumptions. https://arxiv.org/abs/1303.7117 ; https://doi.org/10.1214/14-AOS1252

bibliographic_label: Partha Niyogi, Stephen Smale and Shmuel Weinberger (2008). Finding the homology of submanifolds with high confidence from random samples.
annotation: Discrete & Computational Geometry 39, 419-441. Consulted noiseless reach/density reconstruction statement, especially Proposition 3.1. https://math.uchicago.edu/~shmuel/NSW1.pdf ; https://doi.org/10.1007/s00454-006-1250-7

bibliographic_label: Benedict H. Gross and Don B. Zagier (1986). Heegner points and derivatives of L-series.
annotation: Inventiones Mathematicae 84, 225-320. Arithmetic height/derivative relation with specified hypotheses; not a quantum probability law. https://doi.org/10.1007/BF01388809

bibliographic_label: Thomas Barnet-Lamb, Toby Gee and David Geraghty (2009 preprint, revised 2010). The Sato-Tate conjecture for Hilbert modular forms.
annotation: Primary source for the relevant non-CM equidistribution setting. https://arxiv.org/abs/0912.1054

bibliographic_label: Barry Mazur (1978). Rational isogenies of prime degree.
annotation: Inventiones Mathematicae 44, 129-162; includes the rational torsion classification statement. Primary paper copy: https://www.math.columbia.edu/~goldfeld/Mazur-Goldfeld1978.pdf ; https://doi.org/10.1007/BF01390348

bibliographic_label: Anton Kapustin and Edward Witten (2006). Electric-Magnetic Duality and the Geometric Langlands Program.
annotation: Related mathematical-physics framework; not an ACSC construction. https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-th/0604151

bibliographic_label: Juan Maldacena (1997 preprint). The Large N Limit of Superconformal Field Theories and Supergravity.
annotation: Related gauge/gravity proposal in specific theories and limits. https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-th/9711200

bibliographic_label: Max Tegmark (2008). The Mathematical Universe.
annotation: Foundations of Physics 38, 101-150. Related philosophical proposal. https://arxiv.org/abs/0704.0646v2 ; https://doi.org/10.1007/s10701-007-9186-9

bibliographic_label: J. S. Milne (2017). Modular Functions and Modular Forms, version 1.31.
annotation: Author's course notes; modular transformation conventions and Eisenstein zeros, especially Example 4.15. https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/MF.pdf

bibliographic_label: The L-functions and Modular Forms Database. Elliptic curve 11.a3.
annotation: Catalog record for the small-discriminant conductor-11 example; consulted alongside ecdata, rather than treating labels as a new proof of classification. https://www.lmfdb.org/EllipticCurve/Q/11/a/3

bibliographic_label: John Cremona. ecdata.
annotation: Pinned source commit 25cec5ecfec8b9f016eb1631ac633194c2bed39f, allcurves/allcurves.00000-09999; catalog labels and coefficient vectors used in the elementary counterexample. https://github.com/JohnCremona/ecdata/blob/25cec5ecfec8b9f016eb1631ac633194c2bed39f/allcurves/allcurves.00000-09999

bibliographic_label: Miles Cranmer (2023). Interpretable Machine Learning for Science with PySR and SymbolicRegression.jl.
annotation: Symbolic-regression tooling and methodology. https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.01582

bibliographic_label: Michael Schmidt and Hod Lipson (2009). Distilling Free-Form Natural Laws from Experimental Data.
annotation: Science 324, 81-85. Related experimental equation discovery, not evidence for the historical ACSC fits. https://doi.org/10.1126/science.1165893 .
